name: King's Indian Defense
description: A hypermodern setup where Black lets White build a center, then attacks it with pieces and pawn breaks.

moves.explanation: White starts with a queen-pawn center.
Black develops and watches the central squares.
White gains more queenside and central space.
Black prepares to fianchetto the bishop.
Black places the bishop on the long diagonal toward the center.

ideas: Let White build a center, then challenge it later.
Castle and prepare pawn breaks such as d6 and e5 or c5.
commonMistakes: Playing passively and never challenging White's center.
Opening the kingside before the king is safe.
Forgetting that space disadvantage requires active counterplay.
